request.system:
You are assisting with the qualitative analysis of interview data from a study of frontline hotel employees' work experiences. You will receive one passage from an interview transcript. Code the passage as a qualitative researcher would in first-order coding, and complete the coding form below.

About the passage
- The passage begins with brief details about the interviewee: role, gender and years in the job.
- Lines marked "Interviewer:" are the interviewer's questions. Lines marked "Interviewee:" are the interviewee's answers.
- Some passages contain two excerpts from the same interview, marked [Earlier in the interview] and [Later in the interview].

The coding form
1. codes: Give between 3 and 6 first-order codes. Each code has a short label of 2 to 6 words, kept close to the interviewee's own language, and one supporting quote. Each quote must be copied word for word from the passage, without any change, and must be no longer than 30 words.
2. interpretation: In one or two sentences, in your own words, state what the interviewee is communicating in this passage.
3. tone: The overall tone of the interviewee's account. Choose one: positive, negative, mixed or neutral.
4. confidence: An integer from 0 to 100 indicating how confident you are that your interpretation is accurate.

Respond only with a JSON object that follows the schema provided. Write in English.
request.user:
Interviewee details: Public-area cleaner, male, 4th year

Interviewer: What’s the atmosphere like in your department?

Interviewee: The atmosphere couldn’t be better. Our supervisor often says our department is one big family, we’re all family here. We’re family, after all, so of course nobody keeps score. This Spring Festival I worked twelve days straight. On New Year’s Eve I worked from seven in the morning until eleven at night, running back and forth between the lobby, the lifts and the toilets. We’re family, after all, so of course we should be together at New Year. New Year’s Eve dinner was a box of dumplings handed out by the canteen. I ate it in the store room, then went straight back to mopping. Xiao Li in our team, his grandmother was in hospital, and he wanted to take two days off to go back and see her. The supervisor told him, as family you can’t just walk away from your duties at a time like this, everyone’s holding the fort, if you leave who’s going to cover for you? So in the end Xiao Li didn’t go. We’re family, after all, we have to be understanding with each other. The day his grandmother was discharged, he phoned home from the stairwell, and after the call he stood there for a long time. About overtime pay, someone asked once in the group chat. The supervisor said, among family, talking about money just hurts feelings, it’ll all be considered together at the end of the year. The result of considering it all together at the end of the year was that everyone got a bottle of cooking oil and a thank-you card, and on the card was the word family again. At the end of the year our supervisor was named one of the group’s Outstanding Managers. When he went up on stage to give his speech at the award ceremony, he said what he was proudest of was building a team that’s like a family, that doesn’t make demands and doesn’t count the cost. At that point he even paused to wipe his eyes. All of us in the audience applauded, and I clapped pretty hard. Honestly, a department as warm as ours really is hard to find these days. Xiao Li ended up leaving the following month. His resignation letter was very polite. It thanked the family for looking after him.

"Unspoken Expectations" regarding overtime pay not being discussed. "Leadership Through Shared Values" as the supervisor's approach.
